That last one, with DBAN seems a little over-bloated. If you have Linux on the machine, you don't need DBAN. If you don't, Linux runs perfectly well off of a live USB drive.

Linux usually has shred which will overwrite your drive with random data, then zero everything out for later. Normally, with the shred -vz command, it will overwrite your data with four complete passes of random data, then a fifth pass of all zeroes.

If this isn't good enough for you, the -n option can control the number of random data passes, such as: shred -vzn 2 will give you two passes of random data with one pass of zeroes. You can go down (as shown) or up as you wish. You can also remove the -z option and leave the random data, and forgo the pass of zeroes.
